column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
Why do different people, like a landless labourer and a rich farmer, want different things from development?
Can one group's development be bad for another group? Give an example.
Apart from money, what other things do people want from their lives?
Why might someone choose a job that pays less? What else can a job give a person?
Will everyone in a country agree on what progress for the nation should mean?
What questions should we ask when different ideas of development clash?
Why is total income not a good way to compare countries, and what do we use instead?
How does the World Bank use income to group countries, and where does India fall?
If two countries have the same average income, why might we still prefer one of them?
What important thing does an average not tell us about a country's income?
How do Kerala and Haryana compare on children's health, and what does that show about using income alone?
Can money in your pocket buy everything you need to live well? Give examples.
Why is it often better for some goods and services to be provided for everyone together?
Why do some states, like Kerala, do well on health even without very high incomes?
Is income enough to measure how developed a country is? What else is now used?
Which organisation publishes the Human Development Report, and what does it compare countries on?
What warnings have been given about the way we are developing today?
How can a resource that nature renews, like groundwater, still run short?
What happens to resources that nature cannot renew, like crude oil?
What kind of activities belong to the [[primary sector]], and why is it called 'primary'?
What happens to natural products in the secondary sector? Give an example.
How is the tertiary sector different from the other two? Give some examples.
Do the three sectors work on their own, or do they depend on each other?
Give an example of how a problem in one sector affects another sector.
Why do we count only some goods when we measure a sector's production? What could go wrong otherwise?
What is GDP, and how is it worked out from the production of the sectors?
In the early stages of development, which sector mattered most in today's developed countries?
What changed as new ways of making goods spread?
In the last hundred years, which way has the shift between sectors gone in developed countries?
Which sector's production grew the most in India between [[1977-78 and 2017-18]]?
Give some reasons why the tertiary sector is growing so fast in India.
Has employment shifted between sectors in the same way that production has?
Why have most workers not moved out of the primary sector?
What would happen to farm production if a few workers moved out of agriculture? What does that tell us?
Think of [[Laxmi]]'s family: everyone works, so why is it still a kind of unemployment?
How could money spent on irrigation create more work for families like Laxmi's?
How could better roads or storage create more jobs in rural areas?
What kinds of industries could be set up in semi-rural areas to employ more people?
What does MGNREGA promise rural people, and what happens if the government cannot keep the promise?
What makes a workplace part of the organised sector?
What benefits do workers in the organised sector get?
What are working conditions like in the unorganised sector?
Why have jobs in the organised sector been growing so slowly?
Who works in the unorganised sector in rural and in urban areas?
Which social groups are most often found in the unorganised sector, and what extra problems do they face?
On what basis are economic activities divided into public and private sectors? Give an example of each.
What is the main aim of each sector, and how does the government pay for its services?
Why does the government build things like roads and railways instead of leaving them to private companies?
How does the government support small industries, farmers and poor consumers?
Which services are mainly the government's responsibility to provide for everyone?
What problem would a shoe maker who wants wheat face if there were no money?
How does money get rid of that problem?
Modern notes and coins have no use of their own, so why does everyone accept them?
Who issues currency notes in India, and can anyone refuse to accept the rupee?
Why do people put money in banks, and when can they take it out?
What is a [[cheque]], and how does it let people pay without cash?
Why are bank deposits counted as money in the modern economy?
What share of their deposits do banks keep in hand, and why?
What do banks do with most of the money people deposit?
How do banks earn their income from deposits and loans?
How did credit help [[Salim]]'s business?
What happened to [[Swapna]] after she took a loan, and why?
What decides whether credit will help a rural borrower or harm them?
What is collateral, and what can the lender do with it?
What makes up the 'terms of credit'? Are they the same for every loan?
Where did [[Shyamal]] borrow from, and what conditions did he have to accept?
Where did [[Arun]] get his loan, and how were his terms different from the others?
Who does [[Rama]] borrow from, and how does she repay?
Which lenders give formal loans, and which give informal loans?
Who supervises formal lenders, and what does it check?
What happens because nobody supervises informal lenders?
How do poorer and better-off households differ in where they get their loans?
How much of rural people's credit needs does the formal sector meet, and what should change?
Why is it hard for poor people to get loans from banks?
How is a Self Help Group organised, and how does it work?
Who takes decisions in a Self Help Group, and how does that solve the problem of security for loans?
What is an MNC, and where does it choose to set up production?
How do MNCs spread their production across different countries? Give an example.
What is meant by [[investment]], and what is it called when MNCs make it?
How do MNCs work with local companies, and what can happen to those companies?
How do large MNCs get goods made by other firms abroad without owning them? Give an industry as an example.
How does foreign trade help producers and buyers?
What happened in India when toys from China came into the market?
What happens to choice and prices in two markets once trade opens between them?
What has been happening to MNCs' investment and to trade between countries in recent decades?
What is globalisation, and what has caused it?
How have improvements in transport made global trade easier?
How has information technology helped spread production and services across countries?
Why did India put barriers on foreign trade and investment [[after Independence]]?
What changed in India's policy around [[1991]], and why?
What does liberalisation mean?
What is the aim of the WTO, and who started it?
Do all countries follow the WTO's free-trade rules equally? Explain.
How does the [[US]] government's support to its farmers affect farmers in other countries?
Which consumers have gained the most from globalisation, and how?
Has globalisation affected all producers and workers in the same way?
How have some large Indian companies benefited from globalisation?
What special zones has the government set up to attract foreign companies, and what do they offer?
How have labour laws been changed to attract foreign investment?
What happened to [[Ravi]]'s capacitor company, and why?
Which small industries have been hit by competition, and what happened to their workers?
How have employers changed the way they hire workers because of competition?
How do garment exporters keep their costs low, and what does it mean for workers?
Has everyone benefited from globalisation? Who has gained the most?
What would fair globalisation look like?
What can the government do to make globalisation fairer?
What tricks do some traders use to cheat consumers?
Why are markets often unfair to consumers?
Why did the consumer movement begin, and who was earlier thought to be responsible for a bad purchase?
What problems in India led to the consumer movement becoming a social force?
What major law did the consumer movement lead to in India?
What does the right to safety protect consumers from? Give an example.
What happened to Reji Mathew, and how did his case end?
What details are printed on a product's packing, and why?
What can a consumer do with this information if a product is faulty or overpriced?
What happened in Abirami's case, and which right did it involve?
Give an example of a seller forcing a consumer to buy something extra.
What can a consumer claim if they are harmed by an unfair trade practice?
How can a consumer take a case to a consumer court? What happened in [[Prakash]]'s case?
What do consumer forums and consumer protection councils do?
How are consumer courts organised under COPRA, and how is a case's level decided?
What do logos like ISI, Agmark and Hallmark tell a consumer?
Must every producer follow these quality standards? Which products are the exception?
What problems do consumers face when they try to get justice?
What changes were made to COPRA in 2019?
How far has consumer awareness spread, and what does the movement need to succeed?
